**Make the Intake System succeed — the pre-ticket layer where anyone on the team drops what they noticed (a bug, a gap, a wish, an idea) in seconds, and the coordination work of organizing it, connecting it and ranking it is handled *for* them rather than *by* them.**

The bet: teams under-contribute because contributing costs everyone's time. So separate **writing** — frictionless capture, drop it anywhere, no format police — from **editing**, a regular grooming pass that dedups, connects symptoms to root causes, and ranks what to pull first. Hand the coordination load to the machine; keep every judgment call with a human.

## Where it sits

This project is the system **dogfooding itself**. Feedback about the Intake System — from the expert panel, from the critique passes, and from anyone using it — lands in this project's own inbox channels and gets groomed by the same wave process it describes. If the process can't survive its own feedback, it won't survive anyone else's.

## What it's trying to move

Finchclaims backlog, 2026-07-28, 1308 open issues: **73.8%** sitting un-triaged in Backlog · **77.3%** with no assignee · **43.7%** with no priority · **19.3%** untouched for 90+ days.

Note the honest limit: those figures describe the **state** of the backlog, not the flow through it — they cannot by themselves tell us whether coordination or execution capacity is the real constraint. That question needs the forward test in [FIN-3461](<https://linear.app/finchclaims/issue/FIN-3461>).
